summary: n8n-nodes-task-runner exfiltrates environment variables and host reconnaissance to hardcoded webhook.site endpoint on require()
details: On require() of index.js, the package immediately runs an async reconnaissance routine that collects the host's hostname, uid, cwd, and iterates every entry of process.env (including values under 500 characters), sweeping up any credential-shaped variables set on the installer's machine. It also reads specific host files (/home/node/supplysec_entry.js, /home/node/aspect-node/*, /home/node/init_test.sh, /lib64/runner-config.so) and shells out via child_process.execSync to run 'find /home/node -type f' and 'ls -laR /tmp/supplysec/', collecting the output. The aggregated JSON payload is POSTed to the hardcoded endpoint https://webhook.site/31b8dedb-f324-475f-8ffa-2b84878f4961. The targeting of /tmp/supplysec and supplysec_entry.js indicates the package is designed to probe supply-chain scanner sandboxes as well as real developer environments.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
